The body consists of a short head, a rounded muzzle, a small mouth, a horseshoe-shaped lower half. Beardless with a complete lateral line, it has moderately large round scales. The third to tenth dorsal fin is the longest, then shorter. The tail fin is forked.
Koi is a gentle fish and has a variety of colors. Its body is covered with shiny golden or silver scales.

Inhabits tropical and subtropical oceans, also found in temperate and cold zones. Swims alone or in pairs, sometimes in groups of about 10 or more. The smaller are more active, often jumping out of the water surface, while the larger are slow.
Bluefish is usually found in the middle and lower layers of the water. It rarely swims to the surface. A carnivorous fish, it is the most delicious of the 4 major fish that frequent dinner tables.
Active at night, dormant during the day. Predates on flesh.
The fish is mutated. Since its body lacks protein, it takes other fish for protein supply. Slippery fish are its favorite.

Electric eel lives in slow-moving rivers, surfacing every few minutes to breathe air. Often feeding at night, it preys mainly on small fish, crabs, shrimp, crustaceans and aquatic insects. Animal carcasses are also part of their diet.

Batoids can be found in most of the world's oceans. They live in the mud and sand of the ocean floor. The juveniles feed on benthic animals such as crabs and lobsters. The adults hunt mollusks such as squid.

Swims slowly, usually hovering on the seafloor in a head-up-tail-down position, waiting for prey to swim by and suck into the mouth. A carnivorous fish, its hard jaws are capable of breaking shells. Feeds on creatures including small and medium-sized fish, squid, krill, crabs and so on.
Hammerhead Sharks frequent beaches, bays and estuaries. They make long migrations with the change of seasons. Their diet consists mainly of fish, crustaceans and mollusks.

Tiger Sharks are a warm water fish with a ferocious nature that feeds on fish, crustaceans, mollusks, seabirds, sea turtles, sea snakes, seals and a variety of dead animals. They attack and injure humans.

The loach is found in shallow waters throughout the tropics and subtropics. It is a gentle, calm fish that prefers to swim in groups. Although it has strong muscles and the ability to move quickly, it shows no territorial behavior or aggression. They usually inhabit the bottom of the ocean and sometimes surface to feed.
Giant Mouth Sharks have large heads and mouths with fine teeth in the form of whiskers. They feed on plankton and loaches. The lights developed near their mouths are used to attract prey.

A fierce predator, the Flag Fish often feeds on squid and fallfish. When they hunt, they often break into a school of fish, tear the school to pieces, and then use their long, sword-like snout to crush and slowly enjoy their victims.
Naturally short, easy victim of river drowning. Gululu...
The White Sturgeon is one of the largest bony fish in the world and one of the largest predators on the planet. It lives in freshwater as a juvenile and prefers to eat grasshoppers.
An ancient species of fish that lives in large groups. Most of the time their enemies do not dare to approach them.
An oceanic fish with a mild nature that feeds on plankton and locusts. Mainly seen in tropical and temperate sea areas. Can be found in Chinese seas in summer and fall.

Inhabits the estuaries of subtropical seas where salt and fresh water meet. Takes shelter in shallow water and rocky areas. Gathers near the beach to rest or play. Its daily routine usually coincides with the tides and the movement of the sun, with morning being the most active time and high tide being feeding time.
Great White Shark is found in tropical, subtropical and temperate zones and feeds on a variety of fish.

The front part of the body is cylindrical, while the rear part is flattened on the sides. The body is in grayish-black, while the back and head is in darker colors and the belly is pale. It has irregular black patches on the sides and black stripes on the head.

White-Spotted Dogfish mainly lives in lakes and rivers with vegetation. As a kind of carnivorous fish, it has an elongated body, pointed snout, and forked tail fin. It feeds on fish, crustaceans, birds, and small mammals.

With serrated teeth, Golden River Tigerfish leaves smooth-cut wounds on its prey. It is agile and swift. Distributed in South America, particularly in the Amazon River basin, it is fierce and exhibits strong migratory behavior.

Far East Taimen can either stay in freshwater for life or belong to a migrating population. This migrating population is well-known in the coastal areas of eastern Hokkaido.In summer, they remain in river estuaries, and from mid-September to late October, they return to the riverside to spend the winter.

Starry Pearl Trio Fish belongs to the carp family and is found in the Tumen River system. It has an elongated body, slightly flattened on the sides, a slightly convex back edge, a round abdomen without ridge, and a cone-shaped head.

1. Only heroes with an initial Mythic quality can participate in Exchange. 

2. Heroes available for less than 60 days since the Limited Recruitment started are not eligible for Exchange.

3. After Exchange, the Star levels, Fragments, Awaken process and Levels, Gem slot unlock status of the two heroes will be swapped. Both sides’ mounted gems will be automatically removed and sent to the Gem Inventory. If two heroes have different quality and one of them has already activated Awaken, the hero quality of both heroes will be swapped.

4. Calculation of exchange cost for hero fragment:
   · Calculate the difference in the total number of [hero fragments consumed for star upgrades, owned hero fragments, and hero fragments consumed for awaken] between the two heroes being exchanged. The difference will be converted into Hero Exchange Stones at a 10:1 ratio.

5. Calculation of exchange cost for awakened heroes:
   · Calculate the difference in awakening materials consumed between the two heroes being exchanged. The difference will be converted into Hero Exchange Stones at a 3:1 ratio.
   · If there is a quality difference between the heroes (a Mythic hero and an Eternal hero), an additional 100 Hero Exchange Stones will be required.

6. The final total of all consumed Hero Swap Stones will be rounded up to the nearest whole number.

A tadpole looks for its mother. The story is the same with my wife's.
Catch it in winter, and it will surprise you.
Its body consists mostly of shells and little flesh, yet people like to eat it as food. Crayfish, another popular seafood, is its relative.

Primary habitat is the ocean floor at depths of 200 to 600 meters. Omnivorous, with a predilection for carnivores. Eats benthic invertebrates such as crustaceans and polychaetes. Primary enemies are humans and large predatory fish.

A natural \"cleaner,\" the Island Red Crab digests fallen leaves, and its droppings become fertilizer that feeds the trees. It also often burrows into the roots of trees, loosening the soil and allowing the trees to grow.

Amber Seahorses usually prefer to live in the slow currents of coral reefs because they are poor swimmers and slow movers. However, they are very efficient at catching copepods that are fast moving and good at hiding.

Lives in shallow tropical coastal reefs, hiding in crevices or under rocks during the day and feeding at night. Moves slowly with a spiny carapace that can protect itself from predators. Omnivorous on polychaetes, mussels, crustaceans and other benthic animals.
The Giant Squid rests during the day and swims to shallow waters at night to feed. Carnivorous, it feeds on fish, but also on its own kind and occasionally on seaweed.

Nautilus has undergone hundreds of millions of years of evolution on Earth, but its appearance and habits have changed little. Known as a \"living fossil\" in the ocean, it is usually active at night and dormant during the day on the ocean floor, with tentacles attached to the substrate rock.

Giant China Turtle is amphibious and breathes with its lungs. It lives in clean rivers, lakes, reservoirs, ponds, and other bodies of water, often lying on the shore to bask in the sun during the day when the wind and waves are calm. It is usually very shy and very sensitive to the sound and movement of objects in its environment. Any change in its surroundings can alert it and cause it to return to the water bottom.

With highly developed sensory organs, the Big Eye Squid has two long predatory tentacles with swollen tips and powerful suckers. Sharp teeth grow from the rings of the suckers. Its huge body doesn't make it invincible.

Jellyfish are found in tropical and temperate waters as well as oceans hundreds of feet deep. Shallow waters, even freshwater, can be their habitat. The species is 650 million years old, predating even the dinosaurs.

Oysters are widespread in tropical, subtropical, and temperate seas, but are rarely found in cold areas. When the environment is suitable, they use peduncle glands to secrete peduncles that attach themselves to the attached object. Once the shell is properly placed, they release adhesive materials from the body, thus fixing themselves to the environment.

Horned Salamander lives mostly in the outer sea with high salinity, high water clarity and abundant seaweed. Its shell is gray-brown, hard and thick, with a rounded perimeter. It has 6 layers of shell with a rounded top. The thick ribs and thin ribs of the shell are interspersed with thin scales.

Widespread in tropical and temperate seas worldwide. Occupies caves or crevices in rocky seabeds and prefers to remain hidden. The species is considered the most intelligent invertebrate, with highly developed pigmented cells that can change body color very quickly.

Although it looks like a sea slug, they are actually far away on the biological maps. It belongs to the phylum Platyhelminthes, a family of soft-bodied flatworms with an extremely flat body and a head at the front, making it a primitive bilaterally symmetrical animal.

The abalone shell is ear-shaped, large, thick and has three layers. The spiral part shows little trace and occupies a very small portion of the entire shell. The body shell layer is prominent. The surface of the shell has threads and the side has nine small holes, so it is also known as nine-hole spiral shell.

Sea Cucumbers are found primarily in the Indian and western Pacific Oceans. They rely on tentacles to sweep or grasp the loose sediments and precipitated particles on the substrate. Their diet includes inorganic matter, organic debris, decaying remains of plants and animals, microorganisms, feces of other animals and even their own, tiny organic matter and bacteria, etc.
Sea Snails prefer to live in environments with clear water, open currents, and seaweed thickets. They are most commonly found in shallow tropical and subtropical seas.
The Giant Isopod is the largest drifter in the world. They appeared 160 million years ago and have survived ever since. They feed on the carrion of dead fish and occasionally on algae.

Usually inhabits the area from the subtidal zone to the shallow sea area about 100 meters deep. A good swimmer. Can use the closed shell muscle to open and close its two shells, and do butterfly swimming in horizontal and vertical directions. A filter-feeder, a passive eater, feeding mainly on plankton, bacteria and organic debris.

Lives in groups and often inhabits the ocean floor where there is sand, rock or coral. Carnivores on shellfish, sea urchins, crabs, anemones and other slow moving marine life and even beautiful and colorful corals.

Hairy Crabs live on the banks of rivers and lakes with high water clarity and rich vegetation. They like to hide in the gravel and grass and live in the hole they dig. They feed on aquatic plants, benthic animals, organic debris and animal carcasses.

The Green Crab is a warm-blooded benthic and burrowing animal that hides in its burrow during the day and feeds at night. Crawling on its walking feet and swimming on its swimming feet, it eats mollusks, animal carcasses, and mayflies.

Hermit Crabs generally live in the shallow waters of beach reefs or coral reefs in the intertidal zone and other marine environments. They use snail shells as hosts and carry them to crawl. When frightened, they would immediately shrink their bodies into the shells.

A member of the giant fin squid family, the Fin Squid is a deep-sea creature with large fins and long filaments protruding from the ends of its carpal and antennae, which are more than 11 times the length of its body.

The Flower Shell lurks in the sand or mud during the day, exposing its water tube above the ground, and feeds at night. It moves by crawling, with the help of the mucus secreted by its feet. It has obvious migratory habits.

Rainbow Snails have small, flattened, smooth and shiny shells. The shoulder corners of the body layer are sharp and the shell opening is quite small. The sutures are extremely shallow. A large light gray layer of slime covers the navel cavity, making the bottom of the shell look unpleasant.
Lives from intertidal zones to gravelly sedimentary bottoms at a depth of 10 meters in clean slow moving water.

Sea Urchins are found in oceans around the world, with most species seen in the Indian and Western Pacific Oceans. They live vertically from the intertidal zone to the deep sea at depths of 5,000 meters.

Sea Pig, a type of sea cucumber, have a light peach color and appears semi-transparent. They have some \"legs\" that are actually filtering tubes. When caught from the sea, the sea pig looks very peculiar, resembling a fleshy potato. Due to their fragility, they often break into gelatinous fragments when caught in fishing nets.

Distributed in the southern waters of the Japanese archipelago, Flat-Faced Shell can also be seen in the East China Sea and the South China Sea. They live in tropical and subtropical deep-sea areas, ranging from 60 to 1000 meters in depth. Most of them reside in the bottom layer. But they are able to perform large vertical movements by contracting and expanding the membrane between their arms to swim.

Sea Anemone, found in oceans worldwide, have over 1000 known species. Sea Anemones prefer to live in shallow seas and coastal water puddles or crevices between rocks. Some live in the deep abyss, while giant sea anemones are mostly found in tropical areas.  Sea anemones prefer solitary living, and conflicts or even fights may occur when individuals meet.

Marten's Pearl Oysters live in tropical and subtropical seas, naturally found on the seabed in bays or nearshore areas where the water temperature is above 10°C. The depth is generally within 10 meters, and the distribution range is relatively narrow. Adult individuals spend their entire lives attached to rocks and gravel in reef areas with byssus threads.

Neon Fish like to live in water around 22-24 degrees Celsius. They are lively and docile and live harmoniously in groups. They make good group pets when bred in a quiet and dark environment.

Zebrafish is a microscopic predator. They get most of their food from currents and filter their nutrients. Zebrafish is not picky about its food as omnivore. They feed mainly on crustaceans, small insects, worms and algae.
Mickey Mouse Platy is a mild-mannered fish with three densely packed black spots near its tail, one large and two small, that look like Mickey Mouse's head, hence the common name Mickey Mouse Platy.
Greenlight Fish has a large appetite and an inactive nature. Not good at swimming or chasing prey, it grows in the dark depths of the sea and moves slowly.

Native to the Amazon River in South America, Lemon Fish prefers slightly acidic, soft water and a spacious environment with aquatic plants. Its harmonious and bright colors make it one of the most popular small tropical fish.
Moonlight Fish is the first choice for the beginner who wants to pet tropical ornamental fish. Well adapted to aquarium life, it serves as a popular colorful addition to a mixed tank.
Plateau Salmon is native to the warmer waters of the Indian and Pacific Oceans. It feeds on algae, copepods and planktonic crustaceans, and is particularly fond of small earthworms.
A treasure among fish. Loves to live in clean water. Favorite food is worm sandwich with a touch of spicy sauce.
A predatory freshwater fish with a well-developed dental system. Takes other animals as food, but will also eat plant seeds, water grass, shoots and organic particles.
Sand Shifter lives in shallow water and can change the color of its body. It waits for insects such as dragonflies and butterflies to rest on its body, then quickly catches and eats them.
A fish that can live in a variety of habitats, including rivers, lakes, ditches, marshes, wet fields, semi-saline estuaries, and even coastal areas. Feeds on algae and organic detritus.

Yellow Cross Fish is a tropical fish that is very sensitive to water temperature. If the water temperature is too high or too low, it will die. It is also a carnivore that hunts water lice, water red worms and other aquatic organisms with precision and speed.
Peacock Fish has a variety of body colors and tail shapes. It gets its name because its tail looks like a peacock opening its rear.
Tropical pet fish with a deity vibe that loves places rich in grass and rocks.
I'm waiting here, for you to come back...
Lives in the depths of the Indian and Western Atlantic Oceans. Likes to swim in groups and gets along with other fish of similar size. With a gentle nature, it's also not picky about food.
Also known as Arctic Cod, it is a marvelous creature that lives in the Arctic Ocean with a stunningly beautiful appearance and a unique way of surviving.

Sayid Fish is a rare fish found in the outer Nagarand with a dark purple back and a yellowish belly. The most striking thing about it is that its body is covered with colorful and beautiful spots and stripes.
Often found in still or slow-moving rivers, lakes, and sandy, muddy marshes, it is highly adaptable to its environment. Feeds on insects and their larvae, small crustaceans, plant debris and algae.

The body is elongated and slightly flattened with red, blue and green coloration. The caudal fin is well developed. It inhabits the shallow waters of weedy lakes and ditches and feeds on zooplankton, aquatic insects and their larvae.
A relatively rare fish with a body color similar to that of a watermelon. It lives mainly in the shallow waters of tropical oceans.

A very beautiful ornamental fish with an elegant swimming style, also known as the \"Queen of Tropical Fishes\". It has no eyelids and always has its eyes open, which makes people think it doesn't sleep.
A freshwater fish native to the Amazon River in South America and the rivers of Venezuela, Brazil, and Guyana. It has been introduced into countries around the world as an ornamental fish.

Redface Fish is a common fish that lives in continental oceans. It has a light blue back and a white belly. The most striking thing about it is that its gill covers and gills take on a bright red color that is very beautiful.
Cobra Bass is a shallow coastal fish with a wild temperament. Early juveniles feed on zooplankton and later on small shrimp, minnows and isopods. The adult diet becomes predominantly fish and shrimp.
My fish doesn't hate anything for more than 7 seconds...

Yellow Crest Fish has a wild temperament. The juveniles feed on zooplankton. As they grow larger, they can eat small fish and shrimp. Before sexual maturity, the fish can get along well within the species, while after sexual maturity they have a strong territorial instinct. The male and female mate.

Sea Catfish is found in the northwestern Pacific Ocean at depths of 40 to 60 meters. It usually crawls on the sea floor and does not migrate long distances. It feeds on crustaceans, gills, copepods, cephalopods and small fish.
An omnivorous fish that generally feeds on zooplankton, phytoplankton, mosquito larvae, small shrimp and algae.

Figru Mudfish is a strange fish that lives in the Hellespont. It has an oval body, a dark brown back and a light yellow belly. The most striking thing about it is that its body is covered with unique green spots and tiny spines.

Pacific Barreleye Fish is motionless in most of the time. It uses its wide and flat fins to wait for the appearance of prey like plankton and jellyfish.It stares directly at the shadow of its prey through the eyes above its head.

Living in the South China Sea and the Taiwan Strait, Immortal Fish seldom infringe on other fish nor its kind due to its gentle temperament. It has a territorial awareness and mainly feeds on various microorganisms, small fish, and shrimp.

Distributed in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian, Hubei, Hunan, etc. Pond Loach is a small bottom-dwelling fish that hibernates in deep water crevices and mud holes during winter. In other seasons, it mainly lives in ditches, ponds, and shallow waters with abundant grass and gravel in lakes.

Gentle in temperament, the Red-eyed Carp often moves in groups to forage. It is a low-salinity freshwater fish found in slow-flowing or stagnant lakes and ponds at low altitudes, commonly living in groups. It is omnivorous, mainly feeding on attached algae, plankton, and aquatic insects.

The meat is tender and tasty, with a protein content that exceeds that of chicken. It is the premium freshwater fish and is mainly sold fresh, although smoked and cured products are also very popular.
Breathing is difficult while eating beetles is happy.
The Snapper inhabits rocky reefs with clear, algae-filled water. They swim fast in schools and prefer to eat small shrimps such as mysids, scaly shrimps, hairy shrimps and shelled muscle clams.

Plateau Fugu lives on the bottom of special zones and feeds mainly on coral shells, shrimp and crabs, and other marine life. When in danger, they swallow seawater, causing their bodies to swell into a large, spiky ball that is impossible to eat.

Purple Tiger Fish is also known as the man-eating fish. Its head is a large part of its body with thick bones at the back. The eyes are large, round and blood-red. The mouth is full of triangular, sharp teeth set on short, powerful jaws.

A cold-water migratory fish, it inhabits brackish freshwater near estuaries where the water temperature is low, the substrate is sandy and gravelly, and aquatic plants are abundant. The adults live offshore and feed on crustaceans, especially crabs. It does not feed during anadromous spawning migrations.

Sunblaze Fish grows on the sunless bottom of lakes. It has no scales and its eye function is impaired. When the water level rises, it emerges from the rocks and grasses. Its coarse flesh is tender and delicious.

Lives offshore or at the confluence of river and sea. Prefers the muddy and sandy bottoms. A typical carnivorous fish that feeds on small shrimp, fish, sand worms and clams. It is also a fierce predator, chasing its prey as soon as it is found, regardless of the consequences.
A migratory fish that lives mainly in the middle or bottom of the water. The fugu has a mixed diet, feeding mainly on clams, oysters, sea urchins and so on.
The Arhat Fish symbolizes good luck due to its colorful body and large forehead. It likes to live in slightly acidic or neutral waters and enjoys foods such as shrimp, mealworm, and barley worms.

Fins Fish, found in freshwater rivers and lakes in tropical Africa, is an ancient species of hard bone with primitive features such as tough scales and large blowholes. Its earliest fossil record dates back to the Cretaceous period, which is why it is also known as a living fossil.

Lophiomus inhabits mainly sandy and muddy offshore waters. It is a benthic fish that moves slowly, often crawling along the bottom. Carnivorous on fish and crustaceans, it lures prey with its tentacles and bait balls and then inhales the prey in a single gulp.

Current Snapper lives in rocky reef areas and feeds on a wide variety of food. There is one major characteristic of its feeding process: it often circles the bait a few times to check for reaction, then touches the bait with its head and bites. If it feels uncomfortable, it will spit it out immediately.
Rainbowfin Fish is a carnivorous fish that will eat any prey caught in its mouth, including fish, worms, insect larvae, and frogs. If kept in an aquarium, it will also eat fish or other food pieces.

The Silver Fish are found only in the South China Sea, East China Sea, Yellow Sea and Bohai Sea. Most of them live offshore and feed on plankton, copepods, small shrimp and fish. After the juveniles mature in one year, they swim from the offshore to the rivers to spawn.
Pufferfish often inhabits rocky caves at the bottom of the water, feeding on the surrounding vegetation and sometimes the mud inside the caves.

A warm-water pelagic fish common along the northwestern Pacific coast and in the seas of China, Japan, and North Korea. Follows light at night and lives at different depths between day and night. Feeds on a variety of creatures, including planktonic crustaceans and small fish.

Striped Knifefish is a cold water oceanic migratory fish with no stomach and a short intestine. The orange ones have several natural enemies such as marine mammals, squid, tuna and planktivorous subclass fish. They can glide across the surface of the water when fleeing from a predator.

Blue Parrot Fish inhabits the mixed zone of reef and sand and feeds on small benthic animals, even poisonous ones. Blue Parrot Fish is also a very social fish, and in the event of an unfortunate incident with a fellow fish, other fish will rise to the occasion to help.

The eel is fierce, voracious, hyperactive during the day and dormant at night. It follows light and prefers flowing water and warm caves. It can also swim against currents and find caves to hide from its enemies.

With a fierce temperament, White Perch inhabits estuaries and often migrates upstream to freshwater to feed on small fish, wasp worms, etc. Its spawning grounds are on the near shore of estuaries adjacent to the sea.

Highhill Salmon feeds on plankton, and as they grow they become carnivorous and aggressively hunt, often jumping to the surface in groups to compete for food. They migrate to spawn, and all females and males die after spawning.

The juveniles feed on zooplankton, while the adults feed on diatoms and small organisms. Generally marine, they regularly migrate in groups to harbors and river mouths to spawn each year, and the juveniles often enter river mouths and move to deeper ocean areas to overwinter when it is cold.

Mahimahi is a warm temperate pelagic migratory fish. They often swim out to sea in groups, sometimes appearing offshore. Swift swimmers, they like to gather in the driftwood or floating under the seaweed. Mahimahi is carnivorous, preying mainly on sardines, flying fish and other pelagic fish.

An anadromous or freshwater fish of the Northern Hemisphere, found in the North Pacific and Northeast Atlantic and their coastal waters. Looks silver in the ocean and changes its body color from season to season.

Icy River Carp lives in high altitude rivers. Due to the special living environment, its growth rate is relatively slow and its body needs to store a lot of fat for the long winter. Strong muscles out of exercises are required to survive, so it tends to become sturdy with tasty meat.

Ironback Fish lives mostly in the lower and middle layers of the water that are nutritious, sandy and static, and rarely inhabits flowing waters. It has the habit of swimming in groups. It is an omnivorous fish that feeds on small invertebrates and benthic animals.
Blackmouth Fish belongs to the Narcetes subfamily and is known as a treasure of the sea, its meat is not only tasty but also highly nutritious.
Arapaima is considered the most primitive bony fish in existence today. They have a well-developed tooth-like hyoid bone and can bite with teeth that grow on the palate.
Silver Fin Fish is an omnivorous fish found in oceans around the world. The adults can grow to 2 meters in length and are very aggressive with almost no natural predators.

Mainly found in the Indian Ocean and the Pacific, it often lives on coral reefs. Some also live in deep waters. Not proficient in swimming, it is nocturnal and likes to hide during the day in dark areas of the reef with its belly against the rock to protect itself.

Plaice is widely distributed, from brackish water to deep-sea areas up to 1000 meters. When it reaches around 10 millimeters, it begins metamorphosis. One eye gradually moves to the other side, and it rests on the sandy bottom with the blind side facing down.

Sea Bream is a fish species belonging to the Sparidae family, characterized by a large head, small mouth, and red appearance with blue spots. The anterior teeth are conical, while the posterior ones are molar-like. It has comb-like scales, and the dorsal and anal fins have spines.

Found along the coasts of Europe and America in the polar regions and on islands in the Arctic, it is the freshwater fish that ventures furthest into the Arctic region.  It feeds on chironomid larvae, water fleas, and copepods, and as it grows larger, it primarily preys on flying insects.

Participation Rules 1. The Crystal Throne gameplay is cross-region. Regions must be open for more than 30 days to participate. Adjacent regions will be automatically matched in the same competition area. 2. There will be 4 qualifying rounds each month, held on Saturdays from 20:00 to 20:40 (UTC0). Players can enter the battlefield at 19:00 to set up defenses. 3. The system will automatically select the top 32 tribes based on the total power ranking within the competition zone (tribes advancing to the elite group will occupy the top 16 spots by default). The total power of a tribe is the sum of the highest historical power of all its members. 4. The finals will take place on the Sunday of the 4th week of each month from 20:00 to 20:40(UTC0), with competition held among the 4 adjacent regions. 5. After joining a Cross-Server Tribe, you will match alongside your tribe. If you join a Cross-Server Tribe that is already participating in the Crystal Throne, you can only join that tribe or a local tribe for 30 days, starting from the day you joined. 6. From Saturday 20:00 to Sunday 20:00 during the final week, joining Cross-Server Tribes already participating in the Crystal Throne is not allowed.

Gameplay Rules 1. Each match involves 8 tribes. After the battle starts, tribes will be assigned to different locations on the map. 2. There are 4 types of base structures on the map: a. Main Base: Durability 120, Points 10 b. Watchtower: Durability 35, Points 30 c. Stronghold: Durability 50, Points 60 d. Fortress: Durability 70, Points 150 3. Sieging can reduce the durability of base structures, decreasing it by 1 point per attack. Multiple tribes can attack the same base structure simultaneously. The tribe that delivers the final blow will capture the base. 4. Tribes will earn Points for capturing bases. Points affect the battle settlement for the match. 5. The tribe's main base has 15 minutes of protection after the event starts, during which it cannot be attacked. If the main base is captured, the entire tribe is eliminated, and the tribe’s Points are reset to zero. When your tribe occupy various main bases and the original main base is captured, main base will be relocated and your tribe member will receive a "Displaced" effect. "Displaced": All tribe members' march time is doubled. Effect is lifted upon recapturing the original main base. 6. The stronghold has 20 minutes of protection after the event starts, during which it cannot be attacked. 7. Marching Rules a. Players can move to their own bases or adjacent bases. b. Moving between two bases takes the same time, which is 10 seconds. c. Players can use diamonds to speed up the movement. Each speed-up reduces the movement time by half, and speeding up cannot be used if the movement time is ≤10 seconds.

Battle Rules 1. Players need to set their deployment lineup. If no deployment lineup is set, the arena defense lineup will be used automatically. 2. Each hero starts with 100 energy points. Engaging in battles with other players will consume energy, and reduced energy will lower all attributes of the hero. a. The energy consumed by the winning side is determined by the power difference between the two sides. The greater the power difference, the less energy is consumed. b. The losing side will be defeated, and all heroes’ energy will be reduced to 1. Defeated heroes cannot continue to participate in the battle. 3. Players can revive after being defeated. Each battle allows for 5 free revives and 6 item-based revives (more item-based revives are available in the finals). a. Free revives require a 60-second wait. b. Item-based revives require no wait; use items to revive directly. c. After reviving, all heroes’ energy is reset to 100. d. Players have a 5-second protection period after respawning, during which they cannot be attacked by other players.

Ranking Reward Rules 1. Tribe Ranking: At the end of the match, tribes are ranked based on the Points earned during the match. If points are tied, the tribe with higher total combat power ranks higher. Eliminated tribes are ranked based on their elimination time; tribes eliminated earlier will rank lower. Only players who participated in the match or were attacked during the match are eligible for Tribe Ranking rewards. 2. Personal Ranking: At the end of the match, players are ranked based on their personal points. Defeating one player earns 10 points, and attacking one point of building durability earns 1 point. Players with points >0 will receive personal rewards. 3. Both tribe ranking rewards and personal ranking rewards will be sent via email after the match.

Promotion Rules 1. After the settlement on each Saturday of the first three weeks, the top 2 tribes from the regular group will advance to the elite group, while the bottom 2 tribes from the elite group will drop to the regular group. 4. Beneath the tiles are various rewards, as well as monsters and special events.

5. Click on rewards to collect them.

6. Monsters block surrounding tiles. You can only explore the tiles adjacent to monsters after defeating them. Each monster battle consumes 2 stamina points (regardless of the outcome).

7. You cannot access tiles with roadblocks, nor can you explore tiles adjacent to roadblocks.

8. If you find a Lightning, you can use it to eliminate monsters in the ruins. If you find a Fireball, you can use it to clear roadblocks in the ruins.

9. Lightning and Fireball obtained during an exploration will not carry over to the next one. However, you will receive one Lightning and one Fireball at the start of each exploration.

10. Some tiles hide task NPCs. Complete their quests to receive generous rewards from them.

11. The final floor of the ruins contains an Ultimate Chest. After claiming the Ultimate Chest, you can choose to continue exploring the ruin or end the current exploration and take all rewards obtained.

Once the match begins, a 1v1 random battle will start. The side with higher Stamina will advance.

If two pets from the same player are matched against each other, no Stamina will be deducted from either side. The pet with higher Stamina will advance without any loss, while the one with lower Stamina will be eliminated directly.

If Stamina is the same, the winner will be determined based on Quality and then Level in order. If all are identical, the result will be decided randomly. The winner will be left with 1 Stamina point.

Basic Rules

1.Players must own at least one pet to participate. A pet is considered to have joined a match only when deployed in that round.
 
2.Players whose server opened for 21 days and the team level reached 125 can join.

3.Each player can deploy up to 4 pets per match. Each pet has 2 free deployment chances per day. After using up the free chances, players need to consume Pet Duel Ticket to deploy pets. Free chances reset daily at 5:00.
 
4.All pets are randomly matched into groups. The pet with higher Stamina wins. The winner’s remaining Stamina will be reduced by the loser's Stamina and carried into the next round.
 
5.When two pets from the same player are matched, no Stamina is deducted. The pet with higher Stamina advances, while the other is eliminated. If Stamina is the same, the one with higher Rarity advances. If Rarity is the same, the one with a higher Level advances. If both are identical, one pet advances at random.
 
6.When two pets from different players with the same Stamina meet, the one with higher Rarity advances. If Rarity is the same, the one with a higher Level advances. If Level is also the same, the winner is chosen at random. The advancing pet will have 1 Stamina point remaining.
 
7.Once deployed in a match, pets cannot be withdrawn or replaced.
 
8.Pet Arena is a cross-server mode where players compete against others from their own warzone. When activity is low, warzones may merge with adjacent ones.
 
Stamina Explanation

Match Start Rules
1.The match starts automatically once the required number of pets is met for the round.
 
Scoring Rules
1.Total score is the sum of ranking points earned by each pet.

2.Points are used for leaderboard rankings.

Reward Rules
1. In each event cycle, players can deploy pets to participate in the challenge. Upon completion, achievement rewards can be claimed based on the number of deployed pets. Rewards reset with each new event cycle.
 
2. In each event cycle, players can earn ranking rewards based on the total points accumulated during the challenge. These rewards also reset with each new event cycle.

Contest Rules 1. Tribe Clash is a cross-region gameplay. Tribes in zones that have been open for more than 30 days can participate. Neighboring zones will be automatically matched to compete in the same division. 2. The system will automatically select the top 64 tribes with the highest total battle power within the division to participate. The total battle power of a tribe is the sum of all members' highest historical power. If the number of tribes in the zone is small, the top 32 tribes may be selected instead. 3. Tribe Clash is held every two weeks, divided into Preparation Period, Battle Period, and Rest Period. The Battle Period occurs on Tuesday/Wednesday/Thursday from 10 AM to 10 PM, with a total of three rounds. 4. After joining a Cross-Server Tribe, you will match alongside your tribe. If you switch to a tribe in a different competition bracket during the event, your personal damage data from the previous bracket will be cleared. Matching and Advancement Rules 1. All tribes initially compete in the beginner battlefield for group matching. 2. In each round, the tribe with the highest total damage in each group will advance to the next level battlefield. Those not advancing will remain in the current battlefield. 3. The tribe's total damage is determined by the damage dealt in the current round combined with the percentage of remaining health of the main castle. After the main castle is destroyed, subsequent member damage will not contribute to the tribe's total damage for the round. 4. Tribe's damage in the round = Member damage × (1 + percentage of remaining tribe health × 1.5) 5. At 9:50 AM (UTC0) on the day of the battle, the tribe's participant list will be locked. Members who join after this time will not be eligible to participate in the current round of battle.

Castle Construction 1. Construction is divided into Standard Donation and Advanced Donation. 2. Each donation grants rewards and main castle experience points. Once the experience points meet the requirement, the castle can be upgraded, enhancing the tribe's health bonus. 3. The main castle's level and health bonus are locked at the start of each battle round. Donations made during the Battle Period that increase the castle's level will take effect in the next round. 4. Advanced Donation items will be reclaimed at the end of the event, with corresponding Advanced Donation rewards returned. 5. At 9:50 (UTC0) AM, the tribe's participant list will be locked, and members who join after this time cannot make donations in the current round. (Locked at 5 AM on Monday) Battle Rules 1. Players will automatically use their arena defense lineup as their attack power, dealing damage equivalent to their attack power with each attack. 2. The tribe's total health is determined by the sum of all members' power and construction bonuses. Health bonuses are locked at the start of each round, with power changes and construction bonuses taking effect in the next round. 3. Each attack consumes 1 Stamina. Stamina recovers over time, and will not recover when it reaches the maximum limit. At the start of each round, Stamina is reset to 5. 4. After depleting Stamina, Siege Tokens can be used for challenges. After using 25 Siege Tokens in attacks, each subsequent attack consumes an additional Siege Token. The consumption count resets every round. 5. Each battle grants Treasure Keys, which can be used to open the Chieftain's Treasure. 6. Defeating players grants defeat rewards. Each attack—whether using Stamina or a Siege Token—can defeat up to 3 players. Excess damage beyond that does not count.

Summon Phoenix 1. Players can use the item "Ashes of Ao" to summon a Phoenix to attack other tribes. 2. Each attack grants item rewards, and killing tribe members provides additional kill rewards. 3. Phoenix attack damage will not exceed the remaining health of the targeted tribe. 4. "Ashes of Ao" items will be reclaimed at the end of the event, with corresponding usage skill rewards returned. Chieftain's Treasure 1. Treasure Keys can be used to open the Chieftain's Treasure, granting rewards with each opening. 2. Each layer contains 9 treasures, with 1 treasure holding the major prize for that layer. Upon finding the major prize, players advance to the next layer. 3. There are 9 layers in total. The number of Treasure Keys required increases with each layer. 4. Upon opening the major prize on the 9th layer, players receive an additional grand completion reward. 5. After obtaining the major prize on the 9th layer, players can return to the 1st layer, resetting all treasure rewards. 6. Treasure Keys will be reclaimed at the end of the event, with a certain amount of gold returned.

Base Rules

1. Divine Weapons provide additional attributes to heroes. Each Divine Weapon has its own name, quality, level, rating, base attributes, additional attributes, shape, and other details. Once confirmed, this information cannot be changed.
 
2. Divine Weapons with the same name may have different qualities and levels. Divine Weapons with higher quality and level grant higher attribute values. The maximum attainable level of Divine Weapons depends on the Arsenal level.
 
3. Divine Weapons offer base and additional attributes. Each Divine Weapon’s base attribute types are fixed, but their values vary randomly. High-quality Divine Weapons have additional attributes with random types and values. The higher the quality, the more additional attribute lines.
 
4. Divine Weapons must be equipped in the Arsenal for their attributes to take effect. Different shapes occupy different amounts of space in the Arsenal.
 
5. Each class has its own exclusive Arsenal. Players can drag and equip Divine Weapons into the vault of each class. The attributes of Divine Weapons in a vault only apply to all heroes of that class.
 
6. The initial vault size is 3×4. Players can expand vault space by clicking on the lock icon and using Expansion Tools. The more slots expanded, the more tools required. The maximum expansion is 8×6. Vault sizes are calculated independently per class.
 
7. The Arsenal has levels, which affect the maximum level of Divine Weapons players can obtain. All class vaults share the same level. The vault automatically upgrades when a specified amount of Divine Weapon Crystals is reached. Crystals are obtained by dismantling Divine Weapons.
 
8. Unequipped Divine Weapons are placed in temporary storage with limited capacity. When full, new Divine Weapons cannot be acquired. Players can clear space by dismantling Divine Weapons.
 
 
Forging Rules

1. Forging Divine Weapons requires consuming Mystic Ore, which is obtained by mining Mystic Ore veins.
 
2. Forging takes time. Players can use items to speed up forging or purchase Forging Privilege Cards to reduce forging time.
 
3. There is a limit on how many Divine Weapons can be forged simultaneously. Players can increase this limit by purchasing Forging Privilege Cards.
 
4. The quality of forged Divine Weapons depends on the Forge Level. Higher Forge Levels increase the chance of forging high-quality Divine Weapons. The Forge can be upgraded by consuming Crimson Embers, which are obtained by dismantling Divine Weapons. Privilege Cards can increase the amount of Embers gained per dismantle.
 
5. The Arsenal level affects the maximum level of forged Divine Weapons. Higher vault levels allow forging higher-level weapons.
 
6. Forged Divine Weapons are temporarily stored on the forge platform and must be claimed by clicking. The forge platform has a storage limit, so please claim them promptly.
 
 
Dismantling Rules

1. Unwanted Divine Weapons can be dismantled to obtain Divine Weapon Crystals, Crimson Embers, and Expansion Tools.
 
2. Dismantling is irreversible. Weapons can be locked to prevent accidental dismantling.
 
 
Archive Rules

1. Upon first obtaining a Divine Weapon, players can claim an archive reward. Rewards cannot be claimed multiple times.
 
2. Players can view information about Divine Weapons of all qualities in the archive. Base attributes shown in the archive represent the maximum values at fixed levels.

3. Players can view the number of additional attribute lines for Divine Weapons of each quality in the archive.

Gem Rules

1. Gems grant heroes additional stats. Different gem types provide different attributes.

2. Gems must be mounted into equipment. Gems mounted only affect the hero wearing that equipment. Each piece of equipment can hold up to 3 gems.

3. Gems mounted can be removed without any loss.

4. Gems mounted can be quickly replaced or upgraded directly from their gem sockets.

5. Three gems of the same type and tier can be combined into one gem of the same type at the next higher tier. Gems can be upgraded up to Tier 9. Upgrades are irreversible.

6. Gems mounted can be upgraded instantly by consuming the required number of unmounted gems of the same type. Lower-tier gems are prioritized for consumption. If insufficient unsocketed gems are available, Gem Upgrade Scrolls will be used to fill the deficit. Upgrades are irreversible.

7. A Quick Combine option is available in the Gem Inventory. This feature automatically combines all eligible gems to the highest possible tier in a single operation.

Energy Core Rules

1. Each piece of equipment has its own unique Energy Core. Advancing the Energy Core’s tier enhances both the stats and skill effects of the hero who equips the equipment.

2. When an Energy Core reaches a specified tier and the equipment is mounted with the required gems, enhanced stat bonuses unlocks and skill effects will be improved.

3. Advancing an Energy Core requires Equipment Souls specific to the hero’s class, as well as a set amount of Gem Essences.

4. An Energy Core’s tier can be reset, refunding all resources spent during its upgrades.

5. When all four Energy Cores of the same hero reach the required tier, Core Resonance is activated, granting additional stat bonuses.

Relic Description

1. Relics grant the equipped hero significant attribute bonuses and powerful skills. Each hero may equip only one relic.

2. Relics are classified as Unique or Common. Unique Relics cannot be obtained multiple times; duplicates are automatically converted into a set amount of Relic Fragments. Common Relics can be obtained repeatedly.

3. High-quality relics can be Ascended. Ascension provides greater attributes and unlocks potent skills. Ascension for Unique Relics is irreversible, while Ascended Common Relics can be reset without any loss.

4. High-quality relics can be acquired by Combining lower-quality relics. Only relics that have not been enhanced and are not currently equipped can be used in Combination. This operation is irreversible.

Lost Continent Guide

1. The Lost Continent contains multiple areas. You must completely excavate your current area before advancing to the next. Later areas hold richer rewards.

2. Excavation in each area is done layer by layer. Clear plots below the depth marker to progress to deeper layers.

3. Each dig consumes one Shovel. Dirt plots require 1 dig to clear. Stone plots require 2 digs.

4. Shovels regenerate 1 every 10 minutes. Regeneration stops when your maximum is reached. Purchasing the Benefit increases both your Shovel capacity and regeneration rate.

5. Use Explosives or Drills to swiftly clear large sections of land, including stone plots.

6. After mining a set number of times, you can claim a milestone reward.

Participation Rules 1. The Floating Realm mode is a Cross-Server mode. Tribes from Servers that have been open for more than 45 days can participate. Adjacent Servers will be automatically matched into the same competition zone to compete. 2. The system will automatically select the top 64 ranked Tribes by Total Battle Power within the competition zone to participate. Tribe Total Battle Power is the sum of the historical highest Battle Power of all Tribe Members. If there are fewer Tribes within a Server, the top 32 ranked Tribes by Battle Power may also be selected to participate. 3. Floating Realm is held every two weeks. The event is divided into Preparation Period, Battle Period, and Truce Period. The Battle Period is from 10:00 to 22:00 on Tuesdays/Wednesdays/Thursdays, with a total of 3 rounds of Battle. 4. After joining a Cross-Server Tribe, you will Accompany the Tribe in matchmaking. If a player swaps to a Tribe in another participating section during the event, their Personal Explore Points data generated in the previous participating section will be cleared. Gameplay Rules 1. Floating Realm is divided into two parts: Explore and Battlefield. 2. Players can Use Stamina to Explore the Floating Realm, triggering events to claim Rewards. 3. After 19:00 during the Battle Period, players can Go to the Battlefield, declare war on enemy Tribes, and call upon Tribe Members to collectively attack them.

Match and Promotion Rules 1. All tribes are initially matched into groups in the Beginner Battlefield. 2. In each round, tribes with higher total exploration points in their groups will advance to the next level battlefield. Tribes that do not advance will remain in the current battlefield. 3. Exploration points from each round will carry over to the next. Tribe exploration points can be negative; negative points will not lead to elimination, and tribes can still earn exploration points to participate in ranking. 4. Tribe's Total Exploration Points = All Tribe Members' Exploration Points - Points Deducted from Challenges. 5. The list of participating tribe members will be locked at 9:50 AM on the day. Members who join after this time cannot participate in the current round of battle. Exploration Rules 1. Players consume stamina for each exploration. The higher the Floor No., the more stamina consumed per exploration. 2. Each exploration triggers an event. You can only continue to the next exploration after completing the current event. 3. Stamina will automatically recover over time during the battle period, but will no longer recover after exceeding the cap. Stamina will be reset to 30 points at 5 AM on Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday. Stamina from Support Packs purchased on Monday can be retained until Tuesday's battle period. 4. If you fail to challenge a monster or player, a certain amount of the enemies' supply value will be deducted as a minimum. 5. After accumulating a certain amount of stamina consumption, 3x exploration will be unlocked, allowing you to use 3x stamina and Claim 3x rewards. 6. When exploring the 3rd Floor Floating Castle in the Advanced Battlefield, you will additionally Get 1.2x Personal exploration points.

Floor Planning 1. The Floating Realm is divided into 3 floors. The higher the floor, the better the rewards. 2. Players can advance to the next floor by defeating a specified number of monsters or use an item. After entering the next floor, the defeated monster count is reset. 3. On the 3rd Floor of Floating Castle, you will encounter players from other tribes. If you directly defeat an enemy player, you can plunder one highest quality Attribute Bonus from them. 4. If defeated by other players, you will return to the previous floor. Assistance Rules 1. If players fail to defeat monsters or enemy players, they can Mark them, and Tribe Members can provide assistance. 2. Each event grants a certain initial number of assist chances. For every 30 stamina Use, 1 assist chance is added. 3. If an assisted Battle fails, a certain amount of the Enemies' supply value will be deducted as a minimum. 4. After an event is defeated, the player who initiated the assist can manually claim the event rewards. 5. Players can only assist other tribe members with events when they are on the same floor or a higher floor.

Attribute Bonus Rules 1. Exploring within the Floating Realm grants Beast Cores. All Attribute of Beast Cores stack to Upgrade team Attribute during exploration. Attribute for declared war Battle are not affected by Beast Cores. 2. Each player has a Supply Value. Being Attack by other players will decrease Supply Value, which proportionally reduces the Defense Lineup Hero Battle Power. When Supply Value drops to 0 or when Defeated, you will fall back to Floor No. 2. Rank Rewards Rules 1. Individual Rank: At the End of the event, players will be ranked based on their total Personal exploration Points from 3 rounds. Players with Personal exploration Points > 0 can Claim Personal rewards. 2. Tribe Rank: Tribes earn Points in each round based on their Groups Ranking. At the End of the event, tribes will be ranked based on their total Points obtained from 3 rounds. If Points are tied, the tribe with higher Total Battle Power ranks higher. Only players who Join the matches can Claim Tribe Reward. 3. Both Tribe Rank Rewards and Individual Rank Rewards will be sent via mail after the Match Ended. Ranking settlement takes 30 Time after the event Ends. Exit the tribe during settlement will result in not receiving tribe Rewards. Guessing Rules 1. Guessing will open before Round 3. Players can Select tribes participating in the Advanced Battlefield to Guess. The Guessing content is the champion, runner-up, and third-place winners of this match. 2. Guessing Rewards will be distributed via E-mail based on the player's Correct Guess. Purchase Packs 1. Packs can be Purchased during the Preparation and Battle periods, but not during the truce period.
